BudgetWise: ASP.NET Core Web API + React TypeScript personal-finance training app (.NET 8, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS).

**Conventions:** C#: PascalCase types/methods/properties; camelCase locals/parameters; descriptive names; focused methods; composition over inheritance; C# 12 where appropriate; `var` when type is obvious; `using` inside namespaces. Frontend: strict TypeScript; functional React components/hooks; focused reusable components; Tailwind utilities (no inline styles); semantic, accessible HTML (ARIA, keyboard navigation). Use constructor DI and appropriate lifetimes. Use minimal APIs or controllers consistently; REST nouns/HTTP methods; actions return `IActionResult` or typed results. Validate with Data Annotations; built-in middleware; separate request/response DTOs (immutable `record`s); explicit domain/DTO mapping. XML-document all public classes/methods (`<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>` where applicable); comments explain why. Mark incomplete features `// TODO:` with a clear description.

**Testing:** xUnit; React Testing Library; AAA; names `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; `WebApplicationFactory<T>` integration tests; mock external dependencies. Cover success, failures, boundaries, accessibility, and user interactions—not implementation. Use Testing Library `screen` queries; mock APIs with MSW (Mock Service Worker) or similar.

**API/data:** GET/read, POST/create, PUT/update, DELETE/delete; appropriate status codes (200 OK, 201 Created, 404 Not Found, 400 Bad Request, etc.). Plural paths (e.g. `/api/expenses`); IDs in path, filters/search in query. DTOs for complex payloads; Data Annotations or FluentValidation; meaningful errors; camelCase JSON; proper Content-Type. Use in-memory collections for development/testing; realistic representative data via `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`; thread-safe collections where needed. Models: property-based initialization, navigation properties, appropriate nullable references (`?
